thread:
maria: Quick Q — trying to wire up streaming responses in our RN app calling Redwood hosted API. Browser flow uses fetch() + ReadableStream, but RN's JS runtime doesn't support ReadableStream. Any recommended approach for streaming tokens and keeping auth safe? (CORS for web already handled.)

dmitri: RN doesn't support fetch ReadableStream in Hermes/JSCore. Typical patterns: use websocket-based streaming, chunked responses via server-sent events with eventsource polyfill, or use native bridge (iOS/Kotlin) to stream. For auth, don't embed long-lived API keys in mobile builds. Use short-lived ephemeral tokens from our backend.

samir: For mobile we create an ephemeral token endpoint on server that exchanges user creds and calls Redwood with our service key, returns short-lived token (1-10 min). Mobile then uses that token in Authorization header. If streaming via websocket, pass token on ws connect and refresh by reconnecting on expiry.

maria: Any code snippets? I'm prototyping with react-native-webview + hosting a small webview for streaming but worried about token leakage via localStorage/cookies.

dmitri: Short snippet for ephemeral token exchange:

```js
// server
app.post('/session-token', async (req,res)=>{
  const token = await exchangeServiceKeyForEphemeralRedwoodToken();
  res.json({ token, expires_in: 300 });
});
```

On mobile, fetch this and use in header.

Mobile note: don't store in persistent storage. Keep in memory and refresh on backgrounding.

ios-eng: For native iOS streaming wrapper we expose an API that accepts token and returns stream callbacks. That avoids RN stream limitations. On Android same idea with Kotlin coroutines and Retrofit's streaming response body.

samir: Regarding CORS — browser calls to hosted Redwood must have Access-Control-Allow-Origin set and expose Authorization header. If you proxy via our backend, you can avoid CORS entirely.

maria: For web we already use Service Worker to cache prefix responses. Any gotchas for streaming + SW? I saw Safari kills streaming if chunk size small.

dmitri: Yep Safari's streaming ReadableStream behavior is flaky. Workaround: flush larger chunks periodically, or use multipart/x-mixed-replace style. Also ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and not buffering proxies. For SW, forward stream via Response(stream) with proper headers.

maria: React Native specific: I tried `fetch` and got TypeError: network response body is null when reading `response.body.getReader()`. Is there a polyfill?

samir: There's `react-native-blob-util` and `react-native-ss` older libs, but they are chunky. Another approach: use SSE polyfill like `event-source-polyfill` over xhr. Or use websockets with a simple protocol: JSON per message. Simpler and robust.

dmitri: Also note retries: when streaming you can't blindly retry the whole request — do idempotency tokens or resume tokens. Redwood runtime supports resumable cursors in some setups; if not, chunk the stream and include `last_event_id` to resume.

maria: Good point — for now I'll implement websocket-based streaming + ephemeral token rotation (reconnect). Any security notes on passing tokens in ws URL vs header?

ios-eng: Prefer header or subprotocol after initial handshake. If using ws URL, ensure TLS and short expiration. Avoid storing refresh tokens in AsyncStorage.

devex-bot: FYI we've got a sample repo in infra: https://git.redwood.dev/rn-streaming-example — has native modules + server token exchange.

maria: awesome. I'll try websocket approach and post a small PR. pinging for CR when ready @dmitri @samir :thumbsup:

dmitri: happy to review, tag me.

samir: +1
